name: t23-g4-diag-normal-envelope-lowmotion
description: T23 / G4 integrated workload, two measured minutes after a 60 s warmup (joins staggered 800 ms apart: with all eight handshakes at once under this envelope, four exceeded the 5 s handshake timeout -- see docs/reports/G3.md increment 38), players SEPARATED (~77 m apart), under the NORMAL impairment envelope (100 ms RTT, +/-20 ms jitter, 2% loss; docs/validation.md). Eight late-joining clients on the g4-integrated yard: ground slab, 282 comb bodies (ordinary-edit targets, 64 tooth cuts each), 180 tower bodies (blast targets), one dormant 64-brick giant body, 256 always-awake nontrivial debris bodies (64 within 12 m of client 0, kept awake by the fixture agitator) and 4,096 sleeping persistent bodies. The generated stream fires the giant collapse 1 s after warmup, then 10 ordinary comb-tooth edits/s and one 4 m tower blast per 10 s, each aimed at a persistent body by entity id (fresh geometry every edit). Edits target bodies, not terrain, because a terrain commit is O(terrain) (~300 ms at yard scale; docs/reports/G3.md increment 38). Fail-closed telemetry: warmup-excluded tick/physics percentiles, per-client steady egress vs 256 KiB/s, backlog recovery within 5 s of every blast, memory, body populations, baseline concurrency and 1 MiB/s pacing.
